title: Pebble Lines and In-Situ Gold Targets (Part 2)
content: Part 2 of Summary of Exploration Work - Logirim-Chukudum Gold Corridor. Company: Ophir Company Ltd. Date: 5th August 2026. Author: Collins Asseto, B.Sc Nbi; M.S. Auburn.

title: Part 2 - Pebble Lines Significance
content: Pebble lines act as natural hydraulic traps in alluvial/placer gold deposits. Gold settles alongside similarly weighted heavy material and coarse gravel. Natural Riffles: Microscopic low-pressure pockets where gold wedges and lodges. Paystreak Markers: Guide prospectors to concentrated pockets. Energy Indicators: Pebble size/roundness tells historic water flow speed.

title: Part 2 - In-Situ Gold Target
content: Potential insitu prospect sites identified >=5 km east of campsite. Alteration haloes associated with 320 degree-oriented regional strike-slip fault structure. Gold trap sites along conjugate E-W structures. Foreground hills aligned E-W, background hills aligned N-S. Geological hammer head and arrow head oriented dead north.

title: Part 2 - Alteration Halo Mapping
content: Intense alluvial/elluvial workings mapped within drainage basin. E-W oriented mineralization alteration haloes. Zone measuring at least 1000m x 500m. Scale bar: 0m to 1500m. Red dashed lines indicate bounds of alteration halo heading westwards. East: light colored rocks; West: darker unaltered/natural hue. Alteration products: chlorite, epidote, sericite, biotite clays, iron oxides, decayed sulphides.

title: Part 2 - Alteration Zonation Model
content: Rocks further east = lighter colored (infusing of hydrothermal fluids). How Alteration Halos Form: Fluid-Rock Interaction. Zoning: temperature/chemical changes create concentric shells. Exploration Footprint: halos much larger than actual ore veins. Field Comparison: ~800m east of camp - lighter, highly altered, friable. Closer to camp, west - darker, less altered, more competent.

title: Part 2 - Alteration Zone Types
content: Potassic Zone: High-temperature (biotite, K-feldspar). Phyllic/Sericitic Zone: Fine white mica (sericite) + quartz replacing feldspar (bleached rock). Argillic Zone: Clay minerals (kaolinite) in cooler, acidic conditions. Propylitic Zone: Cool outer edge - chlorite, epidote, calcite. Alteration products witnessed in license highlighted in cyan (signaling gold mineralization system).

title: Part 2 - Trenching Purpose and Results
content: Trenching in alteration zones: exposes fresh bedrock. Purposes: (i) map mineral halos, (ii) trace fluid pathways, (iii) collect continuous channel samples, (iv) measure vein orientations. Trench 001: distinct alteration and potential mineralization zones on surface and subsurface. Trenching is essentially a drilling equivalent on the horizontal plane. Saves money (low-cost check before drilling). Showing alteration halos. Mapping structure and veins. Better sampling and testing.

title: Part 2 - Trench 0001 Alteration Zones
content: Trench 0001 Alteration Zones: White arrow: Clay alteration. Green arrow: Chlorite and epidote alteration. Yellow: Iron, sulphides alteration with magnetism and potential gold mineralization. Trenches 0002 to 0006 showed similar haloes at time of writing.

title: Part 2 - Alteration Haloes in Gold Systems
content: Typical hydrothermal alteration haloes illustrated. Similar zones identified in study area. Detailed mapping for mineralization vectoring planned for September 2026.
